items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I believe Sutherland or somebody had a trombone player who played in the black and tan.

ctx.x: He was dead in that two summer.

Well, yeah, the next summer, that was the fall of 1940, and he died in June. But he was talking how at that time he was still going to sue either MCA or he was suing ASCAP. He was always suing somebody for a million dollars, not paying royalties on his tunes. I mean, he had big ideas like that, exaggerated some things of that kind of, he wouldn't have been due a million dollars royalty, but he figured a lot of people were cashing in on his work, which they did. They never got to be millionaires, of course, but…
Well he said don't leave me here. He said he's always had six, seven, eight, or nine. Yeah, that's right. Yeah. Maybe they just gave him some.
